dossier.architecture: Compact swerve scorer with fixed-heading, two-position-hood shooter and simplified alternating climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve supplies chassis heading for aim instead of adding a turret.
subsystems.intake: Over-bumper mecanum vector pickup feeds a ball-width throat.
subsystems.transfer: Independent compliant rollers reject wrong-color cargo without reversing the whole feeder; larger bottom roller removes a dead zone.
subsystems.scoring: Fixed chassis heading, two hood positions and variable wheel speeds.
subsystems.endgame: After Waco, original maintenance-heavy climber replaced by two alternating telescopic arms with passive angle constraints.
subsystems.controls: Custom coprocessor/ROS vision and pathing; quick-turn aim is refined by camera and resets odometry.

versions: Color rejection added after event one. Climber rebuilt after Waco. Feeder deliberately avoids a large hopper.
dossier.analysis: A useful simplification case: preserve acquisition and shot envelope while moving some complexity into chassis aiming. Their experience with an earlier large hopper informed a shorter, more controlled path.
limits: Only published/reviewed configurations are established; further intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-624 · Independent rejection avoids disturbing the entire transport path
context_documents.body:
# 2022-624: Independent rejection avoids disturbing the entire transport path

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

An over-bumper vectored collector narrows into a ball-width throat. The retained technical account describes independently driven compliant contacts, a larger lower roller to remove a dead region and a fixed-heading two-position hood launcher.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source links collector geometry to centering and the independent rejection stage to removing wrong-color cargo without reversing the whole feeder.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Local rejection can preserve a correctly staged ball and reduce recovery time. The narrow throat must still handle simultaneous arrival and worn cargo; a nominal ball-width gap alone does not guarantee reliable singulation.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test two-ball arrival, wrong-color position permutations and aim/readiness delay at both hood positions.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with CRyptonite at Texas District Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:23–3:14 vector intake and sorter; 3:18–4:44 feeder; 4:48–7:09 shooter and vision; 7:15–9:22 climb; 9:25–11:23 controls
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: A ball-width over-bumper throat feeds compact rollers with a separate reject drive.
The fixed-heading shooter uses two hood positions. Coarse chassis aim from odometry hands off to vision.
Two alternating climb arms replaced a maintenance-heavy original. Gravity and constrained swing help present the next hook.
source_reviews.limitations: Nine inches is a nominal team-reported throat value. The captions describe the Texas championship configuration and do not supply as-built clearances.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Talos concentrated on a short feed path and assigned yaw to the swerve drive. The compact pickup narrows cargo immediately, and a separate feeder drive can reverse a local section during rejection. The simplicity of the mechanical yaw solution moved substantial work into finding the target, turning the chassis and correcting the robot’s estimate of its own pose.
piece_flow: Mecanum contacts guide the ball into the narrow over-bumper throat.
Two compliant entrance rollers and a larger lower contact carry cargo through the feeder, against a Lexan guide. The independently driven front pair can help reject an unwanted ball.
Rear transport rollers deliver into the two-position hood launcher. The chassis turns to target and the roller speeds set release.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The short path puts the throat, rejection station and shooter near one another. A large lower roller occupies volume that might otherwise be a dead spot. The compact build also has to preserve a useful center of mass for the alternating climb and let each arm swing far enough to catch the next bar.

subsystems.name: Vector collector and feeder
subsystems.construction: Nominal ball-width throat, mecanum contacts, independent compliant entrance pair, large bottom roller and passive Lexan on one side.
subsystems.operation: Center the ball immediately and use the local drive to reverse the relevant contacts for rejection.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose a compact throat after prototypes and wanted a faster handoff than its 2019 hopper.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A passive guide removes transmission complexity if the opposite contact supplies enough traction at the least favorable compression.
subsystems.interfaces: Collection direction and rejection timing share the same throat.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test grazing entries, worn cargo and a reject with a second ball at the mouth. Inspect Lexan deflection under compression.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact gaps, speed ratios and sensor dwell unresolved.

subsystems.name: Chassis-aimed launcher
subsystems.construction: Fixed-heading launcher with a two-position hood and differentiated roller speeds.
subsystems.operation: Turn the robot from a coarse bearing, refine with vision, set the shot and feed.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team intentionally kept the mechanical build simple after COVID disruptions and assigned yaw to swerve.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare complete cycle time. Chassis aim can spend time or lose a favorable pickup orientation, but it avoids a separate sweeping launcher assembly.
subsystems.interfaces: A useful hood crossover needs adequate trajectories on both sides of the range threshold.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure turn-to-ready after collecting while pointed away and after a lost target.
subsystems.unknowns: No reviewed shot map or aiming time distribution.

subsystems.name: Vision and autonomous
subsystems.construction: UP board processing, target contours filtered in x/y, ROS paths and NetworkTables communication to roboRIO.
subsystems.operation: Coarse quick-turn uses the estimated pose. Vision corrects target bearing and is also used to update odometry when shooting.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted automation to carry work that the simple mechanics left to the chassis. Ceiling reflections motivated filtering.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A wrong visual update can harm both aim and subsequent pose. Bound accepted residuals and specify how stale vision can be before a shot is withheld.
subsystems.interfaces: Pose, path following and shot authorization share data across processors.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test stale messages, false reflections and recovery after odometry drift.
subsystems.unknowns: No source code or recorded estimator residuals reviewed.

subsystems.name: Alternating climb
subsystems.construction: Two commercial-style reaching arms with hook pairs, restrained using wire and elastic material.
subsystems.operation: Take mid, use favorable robot tilt to reach high and repeat for traversal.
subsystems.team_rationale: The original Waco climb hung up and needed frequent maintenance. The team concluded one arm could support the robot while the other reached.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The loaded center of mass determines whether passive tilt opens a usable capture window. Small mass moves can change that window.
subsystems.interfaces: Restraints must permit reach yet limit the travel envelope in normal driving.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check worn restraints, side load and an incomplete hook catch.
subsystems.unknowns: Arm specifications and measured reliability are unresolved.

revisions: Added color sensing after the first district event. Replaced the initial climb after Waco.
transferable_principles: Let the chassis aim when the full turn-and-release cycle fits the scoring task.
Retain independent reverse authority where one transition needs to reject a piece.
disconfirming_conditions: A narrow throat can cost enough acquisition attempts to offset a short internal path.
Passive climbing geometry can fail after mass distribution changes.
remaining_gaps: Competition CAD, measurement of aim-to-release and loaded climb tolerance.
recommended_images: Request a side view of the compact feeder and Lexan guide, plus an underside view of the climb restraints.
